advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether DC `validate_assignee_exists` should carry Cloud's normalized unique-match fallback tier, or document why DC intentionally rejects variants that Cloud resolves.
evidence: DC does only exact match: `for field in ("name", "emailAddress", "displayName"): for user in candidates: if _user_attr(user, field) == assignee: return ...` then `raise AssigneeNotFoundError(...)` (transport.py:733-740)

Cloud has a normalized SECOND tier after exact match: `def _norm(s): return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "", (s or "").lower())` ... `if target in candidates: matched.add(acct)` ... `if len(matched) == 1: return next(iter(matched))` (acli.py:605-626), documented as bug 9b94 resolving legitimate variants like 'joe-oakhart' for 'Joe Oakhart'
`outbound_assignee.py:113` maps `AssigneeNotFoundError` to `(None, True, False)` = definitively unassigned, so the stricter DC miss becomes a silent no-assignment rather than a fallback
advisory.finding: The DC `validate_assignee_exists` implements only the EXACT-match tier and omits Cloud's second-tier normalized unique-match fallback, so a local assignee that is a common case/separator variant of a real DC user (e.g. `joe-oakhart` vs display name `Joe Oakhart`) resolves on Cloud but raises `AssigneeNotFoundError` on DC, silently leaving the ticket unassigned.

Body: `cls = _dc_transport_class(); assert hasattr(cls, "validate_assignee_exists")` — no call, no return-value assertion, `monkeypatch` unused

ABSENCE: search across tests/unit/rebar_reconciler for validate_assignee_exists finds only the hasattr test and unrelated Cloud/fake tests; no DC no-match assertion
_call_logged emits on failure: transport.py:260-263 `except Exception as exc: logger.warning("jira-datacenter transport: %s failed for remote id %r: %r", member, remote_id, exc)`
test only checks logger presence: line 207 `assert isinstance(getattr(dc_transport, "logger", None), logging.Logger)`
ticket AC: "a TEST PROVES THE LOGGER FIRES, using pytest's caplog to assert the record is emitted and carries both the member name and the remote id when the underlying call raises"
ABSENCE: no caplog usage anywhere in the file (search for `caplog` returns no matches)
advisory.finding: `test_validate_assignee_exists_returns_the_dc_username` documents and is named for the return-value contract (DC must return the username, not True/accountId) but its body only asserts `hasattr(cls, "validate_assignee_exists")` and never invokes the method or checks a return value; the `monkeypatch` parameter is unused.
merged_from: test_validate_assignee_exists_returns_the_dc_username asserts only `hasattr(cls, 'validate_assignee_exists')` despite a docstring promising to verify the DC return contract (that the method returns the USERNAME, not an accountId-shaped value or True). The assertion would still pass if the method returned True, an accountId, or None, so it cannot detect the exact regression it documents. The return-value logic (`return str(_user_attr(user, 'name') or assignee)` and exact-match loop) is entirely untested.

The AssigneeNotFoundError error path of validate_assignee_exists is untested. The docstring and ticket AC stress that a definitive miss must raise AssigneeNotFoundError SPECIFICALLY (outbound_assignee.py branches on `type(exc).__name__ == 'AssigneeNotFoundError'`), yet no test exercises the no-match branch (`raise AssigneeNotFoundError(...)` at transport.py:739).

The _call_logged observability contract is not tested: no test asserts the WARNING is emitted naming the member and remote id when an underlying call raises. The ticket AC explicitly requires a caplog assertion, and this is the entire point of the new logger (seven members swallow Exception at every call site, so the log is the only failure signal). test_dc_transport_has_a_logger only checks the module attribute exists, not that any member emits.

evidence: DC: `if exc.code == 404: return {"status": "already_absent", "key": remote_id}` (transport.py:551-552)
